blocks.text: This video shows how to put an animation from Pixodesk 2D Animator on a plain web page, as a Lottie file. It takes one script and one element. Let's start with the page as it is.

blocks.alt: A heading, and nothing that moves yet. The lottie web player is already in the folder, next to the page.

blocks.text: A heading, and nothing that moves yet. The lottie web player is already in the folder, next to the page. Now for the animation itself. Let's switch to the editor, where a football is already drawn.

blocks.alt: It's a vector drawing, standing still.

blocks.text: It's a vector drawing, standing still. To make it move, let's switch on Auto mode.

blocks.alt: With Auto mode on, every change becomes a keyframe.

blocks.text: With Auto mode on, every change becomes a keyframe. Half a second in, let's drag the ball down to the floor.

blocks.alt: A keyframe appears on the timeline, holding the new position.

blocks.text: A keyframe appears on the timeline, holding the new position. At one second, let's bring it back up.

blocks.alt: Now it falls and rises again, in one second.

blocks.text: Now it falls and rises again, in one second. A real ball speeds up as it falls, and slows down as it rises. Let's set that easing.

blocks.alt: Gravity easing, falling and rising, makes the bounce feel natural.

blocks.text: Gravity easing, falling and rising, makes the bounce feel natural. The animation is ready. Let's save it as Lottie JSON, next to the page.

blocks.alt: The animation file is already there, next to the page.

blocks.text: The animation file is already there, next to the page. Let's load the player, and start the animation, at the end of the page.

blocks.alt: Load animation takes the container, the file's path, and loop and autoplay.

blocks.text: Load animation takes the container, the file's path, and loop and autoplay. Then, let's add the element it plays in.

blocks.alt: The container is this element, found by its id.

blocks.text: The container is this element, found by its id. Let's reload the page, and watch.

blocks.alt: There it is. The ball bounces, on a plain web page.

blocks.text: There it is. The ball bounces, on a plain web page. So, one script, one Lottie file saved from the editor, and one element. That's all it takes to bring an animation onto a web page.
